title: Work-stealing read accelerator to cut tail latency for paginated dashboard queries
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Certain multi-tenant dashboard queries that page deep into result sets intermittently exceed our 99th percentile latency SLO even when the median is fine. Investigation shows hotspots where a small set of shards or tenants monopolize read workers and cause queueing/backpressure for other concurrent pagination requests. Existing fixes (overscan, hedging) reduce some cases but create extra read amplification or cost.

Proposal: Implement a 'work-stealing read accelerator' in the dashboard query API layer. The accelerator introduces a lightweight worker pool that can steal pending read tasks across tenant queues when idle, combined with per-tenant adaptive concurrency tokens and an eviction-aware microcache for prefetched row-segments. The goals are to: (1) reduce tail latency by avoiding head-of-line blocking caused by stalled shard reads, (2) limit read amplification by capping speculative prefetches, and (3) preserve tenant isolation and cost predictability.

Design highlights:
- Each incoming paginated query is decomposed into read tasks (shard-range requests / index scans). Tasks are enqueued in a per-tenant logical queue with priority metadata (page depth, client latency SLO).
- A global worker pool pulls from per-tenant queues. Idle workers may 'steal' tasks from other queues when they meet safety checks (same region, compatible model of consistency, and tenant not marked high-priority).
- Adaptive concurrency tokens per tenant limit simultaneous in-flight reads; tokens are adjusted by an online estimator that uses recent latency and error-rate signals.
- Prefetch microcache stores compact row-segments (compressed, TTL) keyed by (tenant, query-signature, page-anchor). Eviction considers tenant quotas and a score that penalizes high-cost lookups.
- Read-steal decisions are weighted: prefer short tasks (small index ranges), avoid large scans, and avoid stealing from tenants in 'burst mode' configured via console flags.
- Safety: stealing is read-only; all writes or consistency-sensitive reads bypass the accelerator. Authorization/Audit logs record when a worker services a task for a different tenant.

Implementation phases:
1) Prototype: library-level worker pool + simulated queueing (unit tests + integration tests with local cluster).
2) Canary: route 5% of traffic in staging to accelerator (feature flag), collect latency histograms, cost-per-token.
3) Rollout: gated via rollout policy; monitor 99/99.9 pctl and revert path.

Cost trade-offs: engineered to favor short tasks to avoid amplifying large scans. Prefetch microcache size defaults to small (1-2 MB per tenant) and is tunable in Dedicated plans to reduce cross-tenant noise.

Why unique: Work-stealing is an orthogonal approach to hedging/overscan; it focuses on improving worker utilization and preventing queue head-of-line blocking without unilateral speculative reads.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype unit tests for worker-stealing semantics and safe tenant isolation
Staging canary (5%) shows >=25% improvement in 99th percentile latency for deep pagination synthetic workload without >10% increase in read tokens cost
No regression in correctness or tenant isolation (audit logs show no unauthorized cross-tenant writes)
Feature flag and rollout policy exist; clear revert instructions documented
